description: A TwinCAT HMI control that renders SEMI substrate maps (wafers, panels and other SEMI substrate types) from SEMI E142.1 MapData XML, SEMI E142.4 Stream-21 transfers, a compact GridData JSON or an E142 JSON projection, with individually selectable, status-colored dies and features drawn on the substrate outline. Maps of a million dies and more render at full resolution: below one device pixel per die the control aggregates rather than point-samples, so a single failing die stays visible at any zoom, and a tap selects a group with a summary of what it contains. Per-die measurements that are not bin codes - a relevance map, a thermal field, a probe result - can be carried as an ordinary E142 overlay and drawn as a value field.
releaseNotes:
5.0.0.0 - Localization, a new package id, and fixes to the tile and the chart.
      Nothing a view binds has changed: no attribute, event or function was
      added, removed, renamed, retyped or re-defaulted. It is a major release
      because two changes ask something of a consumer. See CHANGELOG.md for
      the detail.

      =====================================================================
      BREAKING CHANGES - read these two before upgrading
      =====================================================================

      1. THE PACKAGE ID IS Ekvip.Cinnamon.Semi.SubstrateMap (was SubstrateMap).

         NuGet does not offer a package under a new id as an upgrade of the
         old one.

         WHAT TO DO: replace the package reference in your engineering
         project. The control namespace is unchanged -
         TcHmi.Controls.CNM_UIControls.SEMI.* - so no view needs editing.

      2. LOCALIZATION KEYS NAME THE SLOT THEY FILL, NOT THE ENGLISH TEXT.

         A key is now SubstrateMapBinChart.displayName or category.Data, where
         it used to be the whole English string - in one case a thousand
         characters long.

         WHAT TO DO: only if something of yours reads this package's
         .localization files by key, update the keys. Views and the controls
         themselves are unaffected.

      =====================================================================
      New
      =====================================================================

      - en-US, en-UK and de-DE are supplied, with en-US as the default. The
        strings the controls draw follow the locale: the filter bar's labels,
        options and radius readout, and the chart's remainder bucket. BIN CODES
        ARE NOT TRANSLATED - they are the document's own data, and translating
        them would make a chart disagree with the map beside it.

      - The controls appear in the Toolbox under "Cinnamon SEMI".

      - Every E142_* diagnostic code is documented with a likely cause and what
        to do about it, and where the control recovers by itself the entry says
        so (README.md, "Diagnostic codes").

      - ARCHITECTURE.md (how the controls and the engine fit together), API.md
        (five symptoms, each with the file and call chain to break on),
        CONTRIBUTING.md, and worked examples with screen captures in README.md.
        The shipped text is US English throughout; en-UK is the deliberate
        exception.

      =====================================================================
      Fixed
      =====================================================================

      - THE TILE AND THE CHART IGNORED E142MapData AND E142MapDataJson. Both
        declared the attributes and built their grid from GridData only, so a
        tile bound to a valid E142 document showed "no data" while holding it.
        Both now read all three inputs by the route the map uses, and agree
        with it on all 58 document fixtures.

      - The stale marking and the age text were drawn at the wrong size on any
        display whose device pixel ratio is not 1 - the dashed border appeared
        as a small box near the top-left corner. On a ratio-1 display nothing
        changes.

      - A long substrate identity ran into the chart's timestamp. The identity
        is now shortened with an ellipsis; the timestamp never is.

      - A tile kept a selection it never reported. A control that does not
        select now declines before hit-testing.

      - The share chart drew its legend over its own header.

      - Three diagnostic messages - E142_JSON_UNKNOWN_MEMBER,
        E142_XML_SUBSTRATE_TYPE_UNKNOWN and E142_XML_INTEGRITY - cited internal
        numbers in their text and now state the reason. THE CODES ARE
        UNCHANGED: match on the code, never on the message.

      =====================================================================
      Previous releases
      =====================================================================

      4.0.0.0 - Dashboard widgets, spatial filters, and a golden-map comparison.
      Three new controls and a filter pipeline over the existing map. See
      README.md for the attributes, CHANGELOG.md for the upgrade
      detail, and WIDGET-PATTERN.md if you are giving another control a widget.

      =====================================================================
      BREAKING CHANGES - read these three before upgrading
      =====================================================================

      1. AN UNBOUND CONTROL DRAWS A NO-DATA IMAGE, NOT A DEMO WAFER.

         3.0 drew a sample wafer when nothing was bound. It looked like data, and
         on more than one panel it was taken for data. 4.0 draws an explanatory
         image instead, in the theme's own colors.

         WHAT TO DO: if you relied on the demo appearing in a running view - a
         placeholder, a screenshot, a training panel - set ShowDemoItems="true"
         explicitly. It is off by default. A view that always binds data is
         unaffected.

      2. A VIEW BINDING AN OUTLINE *AND* ShowDemoItems NOW DRAWS THE DEMO.

         Binding an outline used to suppress the demo, so the flag did nothing
         and the panel showed an empty substrate. That was a defect: the flag was
         on and nothing honored it. The demo now draws INSIDE the bound outline,
         scaled to fit it.

         WHAT TO DO: if such a panel is meant to be empty, turn ShowDemoItems
         off. It is the flag that was being ignored and it now does what it says.
         Real bound items still suppress the demo; only the EMPTY case changed.

      3. BIN CODES WITH NO BinQuality AND NO StatusColorMapping ENTRY GET A
         COLOR.

         Such a code used to fall through to the unknown color, so eight sort
         grades rendered as eight identical grays. Each now takes a distinct
         color from a categorical palette with a measured minimum perceptual
         separation.

         WHAT TO DO: if you relied on unqualified codes being visually merged,
         declare a StatusColorMapping entry giving them the same color
         explicitly. Relying on the merge was relying on a limitation.

         A MAP WHOSE CODES ALL CARRY BinQuality RENDERS BYTE-IDENTICALLY TO
         BEFORE. Quality coloring still wins over the categorical fallback, so
         the common case does not move.

      4. onItemSelected IS RAISED AFTER THE ATTRIBUTES IT DESCRIBES.

         It used to be raised BEFORE SelectedItemId, SelectedItemStatus and
         SelectedItems were written, so a handler reading them got the PREVIOUS
         selection - and on the first click of a session there was none, so it
         read null. It looked intermittent because re-clicking the same cell
         leaves the attributes unchanged and only a click on a NEW cell showed
         it.

         WHAT TO DO: if you built a workaround - a one-click delay, a second
         read, ignoring the first event - remove it. If you read the event's own
         payload rather than the attributes, nothing changes for you: the payload
         was always correct.

         Ordering is the only change. The event fires once per click as before,
         with the same payload.

      =====================================================================
      New - three controls
      =====================================================================

      - SubstrateMapWidget: a dashboard tile. A map with nine attributes rather
        than a container holding one. It keeps the last map that RENDERED when a
        feed stops, ages it, and marks itself stale with a dashed border - not a
        tint, because every color on the tile is data. A click raises
        onSubstrateSelected with enough to open the full view. No cell-level hit
        test: at 200 px a die is a fraction of a pixel.

      - SubstrateMapBinChart: bins counted, as bars or as proportions. ONE
        control for both - ChartStyle is "Bars" or "Share" - because they consume
        identical data and differ only in geometry. Bars are descending by count
        and linear FROM ZERO: with yield data the distance to zero is the
        information. Nine categories plus a remainder, and every bar is the
        color the map paints for that code.

      - SubstrateMapFilterBar: selectors that drive a map's filters through a
        binding. It renders no map and holds none - it is the only control in the
        package that WRITES. It never offers an illegal filter/channel pairing;
        it grays the kernel out and says why.

      Each takes the SAME map attributes SubstrateMap takes, bound by you - not a
      reference to a sibling control by id. An id coupling points silently at
      nothing the moment someone moves the map to another page.

      =====================================================================
      New - spatial filters
      =====================================================================

      - SpatialFilter (new, default "None"): "Median", "Min", "Max", "Box" or
        "Gauss" over the aggregated image, with SpatialFilterRadius in device
        pixels.

        Median removes scattered single-cell noise without moving an edge. Max
        dilates - it makes a faint scratch unmistakable, and on a noisy wafer it
        will wall the substrate in, which is a property of the operation and not
        a defect. Min erodes. Box and Gauss smooth a scalar field.

      - FieldView (new, default "Bins"): "Bins", "FailDensity" or "ValueField".

        EIGHT OF THE EIGHTEEN PAIRINGS ARE ILLEGAL. Median, Min and Max pick or
        order palette indices - the median of two categories is a category. Box
        and Gauss average, and the average of two bin indices is not a bin. Bind
        an illegal pair and the control reports E142_FILTER_NOT_APPLICABLE and
        filters nothing; it does not silently substitute. The table is in
        README.md.

      - FILTERS NEED THE MAP TO BE AGGREGATING. They run over the aggregated
        bitmap, which is what makes them cheap - one pass over what is on screen
        rather than over a million cells. Above one device pixel per die there is
        nothing to filter. Zoom out and a filter engages; zoom in and it stops.

        Measured over 640 000 device pixels: Median, Min and Max cost 20 ms at
        radius 1, 28 ms at radius 2, 63 ms at radius 5. Box and Gauss cost 82,
        114 and 187 ms - they convolve a float field rather than pick from a
        histogram. This is PER VIEW CHANGE, not per frame: the layer cache key
        includes the filter, so panning a filtered map costs nothing further.

      =====================================================================
      New - the golden map
      =====================================================================

      - ReferenceGridData and ReferenceMode (both new): compare a map against
        another and gray out what matches.

        The useful reference is NOT a perfect wafer. It is one carrying what the
        substrate is SUPPOSED to contain - test dies, dummy dies, process-control
        structures - which bin as defects by design and are not defects. Bind it
        and they gray out; what stays lit is what is actually wrong.

        Compared by bin CODE rather than by table index, so a reference whose bin
        table is ordered differently still matches.

      =====================================================================
      New - age and staleness
      =====================================================================

      - MapTimestamp (new): the same attribute on the map, the tile and the
        chart, so ONE SYMBOL drives all three. Where it is unbound, a control
        shows when the payload ARRIVED instead and says which clock it used -
        "measured 09:15:00 CEST" against "received 11:59:30 CEST". They are
        different facts: a map that arrived a second ago may describe a wafer
        tested this morning.

        AN E142 DOCUMENT CARRIES NO TIMESTAMP OF ITS OWN. The ITEMVERSION the
        standard defines belongs to the Stream 21 message that transports the
        item, not to the map, so a control that only sees the document cannot
        know when it was made. Bind it from wherever your transport keeps it.

      - StaleAfterSeconds (new, tile): marks a tile whose data has stopped
        arriving. STALENESS IS THE ABSENCE OF AN EVENT and cannot be observed, so
        the control wakes to check - at a rate DERIVED from your threshold, a
        tenth of it, floored at one second and capped at a minute. A fifteen-
        minute takt is not polled every second and a one-second takt is not
        polled every minute. Nothing runs at all when no threshold is set.

      =====================================================================
      Fixed
      =====================================================================

      - Every control's Description.json now states the package version. Base,
        widget, chart and filter bar read 0.0.1.0 while the package read 4.0.0.0.
        The 2.0 notes recorded fixing this class of drift once already; a gate
        now compares the nuspec, every descriptor AND the version these notes
        lead with, so it cannot come back silently.

      =====================================================================
      Previous releases
      =====================================================================

      3.0.0.0 - Level-of-detail aggregation, group selection, and a JSON API.
      Two development cycles since 2.0.0.0: the JSON representation work and the
      LOD aggregation work. See README.md for the features and the reasoning
      behind them.

      =====================================================================
      BREAKING CHANGE - read this one before upgrading
      =====================================================================

      1. A TAP ON A SMALL DIE NOW RAISES onGroupSelected, NOT onItemSelected.

         When dies are drawn smaller than TouchTargetSize (new, default 40 CSS
         pixels), a tap selects a GROUP of dies rather than one, and the control
         raises .onGroupSelected with a summary instead of .onItemSelected. The
         two events never both fire, so a view that binds only .onItemSelected
         goes silent on those maps.

         MEASURE YOUR OWN VIEWS BEFORE UPGRADING. On the reference page shipped
         with this control, ALL SEVEN map panels are affected - their dies are
         16 to 38 CSS pixels, every one below the 40 px default:

           panel              grid     die size     after upgrade
           GridData           13x11     16.1 px     groups 3x3
           GridDataCoord       5x4      37.8 px     groups 2x2
           E142Xml            11x8      19.2 px     groups 3x3
           Frame               8x8      34.6 px     groups 2x2
           Transfer            4x4      37.8 px     groups 2x2

         ITEMS ARE NOT AFFECTED. An item hit still wins outright and still
         raises .onItemSelected, because grouping is about dies being too small
         to tap and an item is not a die.

         WHAT TO DO: bind .onGroupSelected as well. Its data carries the group
         id, the cell count, the worst severity present, and a histogram of the
         ten most common bin codes with the rest as a remainder. Call
         readGroupMembers(id) when you need the individual cells - it returns a
         Uint32Array of cell indices and is deliberately NOT in the payload,
         because a 12 900-cell group as a list of objects is about 1.5 MB, built
         and serialized on every tap.

         TO KEEP THE OLD BEHAVIOR EXACTLY: set TouchTargetSize to 0. That is the
         only value that turns grouping off, and every tap then selects one die
         and raises .onItemSelected as before. The 24 CSS px floor - WCAG 2.2
         SC 2.5.8, Target Size (Minimum) - still applies to every POSITIVE value,
         so a negative number or a 10 clamps to 24; zero is the absence of a
         target rather than a small one.

         A selected group is drawn: its member cells take the same 2 px selection
         ring a single die gets, so a tap always leaves a visible mark.

      =====================================================================
      Changed rendering - the same document can look different
      =====================================================================

      2. BELOW ONE DEVICE PIXEL PER DIE, THE MAP NOW AGGREGATES.

         2.0 point-sampled: each pixel picked ONE die and painted it, so every
         other die in that pixel was invisible, and which one survived depended
         on where the grid happened to land relative to the pixel raster. On a
         600x600 map at 20 dies per pixel a single failing die was invisible at
         EVERY subpixel phase - not bad luck, a certainty.

         3.0 scatters instead: every die reaches the pixel it falls in and the
         pixel is reduced. The same failing die is visible at every factor and
         every phase.

         Aggregated tiles are painted from a SEPARATE, darker palette so an
         operator can tell a summary from a datum. AggregationFactor and
         AggregationMode (both new, read-only) report what the last frame did.

         You are affected if you have baselined screenshots of a zoomed-out map.
         A map whose dies are at least one device pixel across renders exactly
         as before.

      3. DECORATED CELLS ARE MARKED UNDER AGGREGATION.

         Overlay decorations draw as corner wedges above 6 pixels per die and
         stopped entirely below that, so a map with three overlays looked like a
         map with one. An aggregated tile whose bucket carries a decoration is
         now drawn at reduced alpha - same color, substrate showing faintly
         through - so the marks are not silently lost.

      =====================================================================
      New - JSON representation (nothing existing changes)
      =====================================================================

      - E142MapDataJson (new): bind an E142 document as JSON instead of XML.
        Same model, same validation, same errors - for systems that would
        rather not carry an XML parser.

      - toGridData() (new function): export the bound map as compact GridData
        JSON. toE142Xml() is unchanged.

      - The two representations are held to parity by the build: every XML test
        fixture has a JSON counterpart or a registered exemption, and 58 XML /
        77 JSON fixtures round-trip through both transports.

      =====================================================================
      New - aggregation and selection
      =====================================================================

      - AggregationReducer (new, default "Auto"): which reduction an aggregated
        tile uses. "MaxSeverity" paints the worst die in the pixel - it never
        hides a lone defect but saturates on a noisy wafer. "FailFraction"
        paints how much of the pixel failed - it never floods but reduces a
        scratch to a tint.

        "Auto" MEASURES which is happening rather than inferring it from the
        zoom, because the zoom does not determine it: at one aggregation factor
        the chance a pixel holds a failing die runs from 0.5 % to 100 % with the
        defect rate. Each frame measures its own saturation and selects for the
        next, switching up at 0.6 and back at 0.4. The measurement is free - the
        reducer that just ran has already accumulated it.

      - TouchTargetSize (new, default 40 CSS px): how small a die has to be
        before a tap selects a group. Floors at 24. See the breaking change.

      - onGroupSelected (new event), readGroupMembers() (new function).

      - BinQualityAliases (new): map your own vocabulary onto E142 BinQuality,
        so a document spelling it "GOOD" or "P" can be read without editing it.

      - BinSeverityPriority (new): your own ordering of bin codes for the
        MaxSeverity reduction, when the standard's pass/fail/unknown ladder is
        not the ordering that matters on your line.

      =====================================================================
      New - two injection seams, both inert until used
      =====================================================================

      - VALUE FIELDS. An E142 overlay may be given the role "valueField" in
        E142Overlays and is drawn as a lightness-ordered ramp over its own
        BinDefinitions instead of the bin palette. It is for a per-die
        measurement the bin codes cannot express - an LRP relevance map, a
        thermal field, a probe result.

        NOTHING IS ADDED TO THE E142 DOCUMENT. Table 9 already defines MapName
        as "a name that describes the purpose of the bin codes in the map", with
        SortGrade and DefectCode among its own examples, so a quantized
        measurement written as an Overlay named "Relevance" is ordinary
        conformant E142. The role is interpretation on the control's side only.

      - ViewTransform (new) and MapScale (new, read-only): an affine transform
        composed into the view as six components - zoom, pan, rotation, mirror,
        shear. GEOMETRY ONLY; it cannot carry a per-die value, which is what
        value fields are for.

        It is post-multiplied, so its translation is in MILLIMETERS of the
        substrate frame and its scaling is anchored at the canvas center. Read
        MapScale to convert: millimeters = pixels / MapScale.

      =====================================================================
      Fixed
      =====================================================================

      - A single failing die is no longer lost at zoom (see 2).
      - Overlay decorations are no longer silently dropped at zoom (see 3).
      - Physical StepSize is now exercised by the test corpus at three device
        pitches in all four BinTypes. NOTE: the four E142 panels on the shipped
        reference page carry no Layout element at all and render at a constant
        5 mm fallback pitch, so they do not demonstrate physical scale. Adding a
        Layout with a real StepSize to those documents would fix it; the page is
        yours and this release does not touch it.

      =====================================================================
      Limits - documented so they are supported rather than discovered
      =====================================================================

      - THE ITEM PATH DOES NOT AGGREGATE AND DOES NOT SCALE. Measured: 1 000
        items build in 10 ms and 1.7 MB, 10 000 in 30 ms and 21 MB, 100 000 in
        701 ms and 145 MB. THE SUPPORTED CEILING IS 10 000 ITEMS. Nothing in
        this release raises it and nothing was intended to - items are
        individually identified, hit-tested and styled, so there is no bucket
        that could stand for several of them the way a tile stands for a
        thousand dies. If you have more than ten thousand things to draw, they
        are dies rather than items: put them in a GridData or an E142 overlay.

      - Aggregation requires a layer cache. A control rendering without one uses
        the run strategy at any zoom, whatever AggregationFactor reports.

      =====================================================================
      Previous releases
      =====================================================================

      2.0.0.0 - SEMI E142 model coverage, export fidelity and selection detail.
      See README.md for the per-object conformance matrix.

      =====================================================================
      BREAKING CHANGES - read these two before upgrading
      =====================================================================

      1. toE142Xml() EMITS A DIFFERENT DOCUMENT SHAPE.

         For the same bound map, the exported XML now carries a two-level layout
         tree instead of one flat layout:

           1.0                             2.0
           one <Layout>                    two: a top-level 1x1 substrate layout
                                           plus a child device layout
           LayoutSpecifier="L0"            LayoutSpecifier="L0/L0_Devices"
           no <Substrates> block           <Substrates> with the substrate identity

         Both forms are schema-valid and any conforming E142 reader accepts either.
         You are affected only if something downstream byte-compares exported
         documents, or matches on the LayoutSpecifier VALUE rather than resolving
         it. If your exports go to another E142 reader or to a human, nothing
         changes for you.

         Why it changed: E142 Table 2 puts the substrate at Dimension 1x1 with the
         devices in a child layout. The 1.0 output conflated the two and emitted no
         substrate identity at all, so LotId, GoodDevices, AliasIds and the carrier
         fields were lost on every export. Keeping the old shape would have meant
         keeping that defect.

      2. A MAP WITH LID-ONLY BIN CODES NOW RENDERS MORE CELLS.

         <BinCode> entries carrying only a LID, with no X/Y, were dropped by 1.0 -
         it said so, with the warning E142_XML_LID_ONLY_EXCLUDED. They are now
         resolved against the declared lattice and drawn. The same document
         therefore shows cells that were previously blank, and the warning no
         longer fires.

         You are affected only if you have baselined screenshots or cell counts for
         such a document. A map whose bin codes all carry X/Y is unchanged.

      =====================================================================
      NOT breaking - every new behavior is off by default
      =====================================================================

      - ViewSubstrateSide (new) defaults to "follow-map": nothing mirrors. A
        BottomSide map can now be rendered mirrored, but ONLY once this attribute
        is moved off that default. SubstrateSide on its own has never mirrored
        anything and still does not - the coordinate consequences of the other face
        are already carried by OriginLocation and AxisDirection.
      - E142Overlays (new) defaults to null: single-overlay rendering, exactly as
        before. The decoration render pass is skipped entirely.
      - E142AlignToReferenceDevices remains off by default; placement is unchanged
        unless it is explicitly enabled.
      - No attribute was removed, retyped or re-defaulted; no event or callable was
        removed; nothing that parsed in 1.0 fails in 2.0. Verified by running both
        versions over the full 63-document test corpus.

      =====================================================================
      NEW
      =====================================================================

      - Substrate alias identifiers (AliasIds) and the carrier fields CarrierType,
        CarrierId, SlotNumber and SubstrateNumber, exposed as read-only Map*
        attributes and preserved on export.
      - Location identifiers (LID) on bin codes and device ids, carried verbatim as
        join keys and reported on selection. A LID-only map resolves against the
        declared lattice; one with no lattice at all is refused rather than guessed.
      - TransferMap: substrate-to-substrate traceability. A selected cell reports
        where its device came from - source substrate type and id, plus either a
        coordinate or a location identifier on that source.
      - DeviceDataMap with the embedded SEMI E138 PVSet payload. All sixteen PVType
        alternatives are read, including the recursive Su and Arr and the explicit
        NoValue, which stays distinct from xsi:nil and from an empty string.
      - Multi-overlay composition: E142Overlays takes an ordered list of one base
        plus decorations, which draw as per-cell marks over the base fill.
      - ViewSubstrateSide and MapSubstrateSide; E142SubstrateId,
        E142LayoutSpecifier, E142OverlayVersion and E142DeviceDataOverlayName for
        selecting a map in a multi-substrate document; MapSubstrateCount.

      =====================================================================
      EXPORT FIDELITY
      =====================================================================

      toE142Xml now preserves the frame, orientation, substrate side, overlay name
      and version, step size, device size, the source layout tree, bin definitions,
      the full substrate identity including alias ids and carrier fields, and
      resolvable transfer maps. What it does NOT preserve is listed explicitly in
      README.md with the reason for each: device-id maps, device data, per-cell
      LIDs, reference devices, every substrate but the rendered one, and any
      transfer whose source reference cannot be satisfied.

      =====================================================================
      SELECTION
      =====================================================================

      The onItemSelected cell payload and SelectedItems gain lid, deviceId, the five
      transfer fields, deviceData joined to its parameter names by index, and
      per-overlay bin codes for a composed map. Three previously undeclared or
      wrongly typed fields in the SelectionList schema were corrected.

      =====================================================================
      FIXES
      =====================================================================

      - The E142AlignToReferenceDevices descriptor no longer claims a behavior the
        control does not have; it is opt-in and off by default, and says so.
      - The package version was inconsistent between Description.json (0.1.0.0) and
        the nuspec (1.0.0.0). Both now read 2.0.0.0.
      - Documentation: the ITEMTYPE discussion, which stated the well-known name was
        unsettled, now cites [E142.04-RQ-00006-00], which has fixed it since
        October 2022.
      - Source comments and JSDoc were rewritten in plain English throughout, with
        every rule stating whether the standard settles it, the XSD declares it, or
        it is inferred.
title: Cinnamon SEMI SubstrateMap
